chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from a man who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the camel which a man offers as a sacrifice, so it either breaks (a body part), or it perishes. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If his sacrificial animal was ensured (liable for loss), so upon him would be (another one) in its place; and if it did not happen to be ensured, so there is nothing upon him'. I said, 'And can he eat from it?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes'.

key_terms.الْبَدَنَةِ: The female camel (often used for sacrifice)
key_terms.هَدْياً: Sacrificial animal offered for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a sacrificial camel dies before slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the liability for a sacrificial animal (hady) that perishes before slaughter, distinguishing between 'ensured' (daman) and 'non-ensured' states to determine if a replacement is required. It further establishes the permissibility of consuming the meat of the sacrificed animal even if it dies before the formal slaughter, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the transfer of risk and ownership in pilgrimage rituals. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in Hajj and Umrah obligations, ensuring that the pilgrim is not unduly burdened by unforeseen losses of their offering.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from a man who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the camel which the man offers as a sacrifice, so it either breaks (a body part), or it perishes. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his sacrificial animal was ensured, so upon him would be (another one) in its place; and if it did not happen to be ensured, so there is nothing upon him’. I said, ‘And can he eat from it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from a man who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who offers a badanah but it suffers damage or is destroyed. He (the Imam) said, ’If it is a binding obligation, he owes its replacement, otherwise, he is not obligated for anything in this matter.’ I then asked, ‘Can he use it for food?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so.’”
